diagram_candidates.kind: TikZ tower and induction/restriction functor diagram
diagram_candidates.why: The definition gives a degree-raising inclusion, central content blocks, and residue induction/restriction between adjacent contents, with distinct supported and ambient towers. A compact map diagram would make these relationships easier to follow.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Draw adjacent block nodes H^Λ_α and H^Λ_{α+α_i}; label ι_{α,α_i}: H^Λ_α→H^Λ_{α+α_i} and u_{α,i}=Σ_{j_{d+1}=i}e(j). Below them draw e_i: H^Λ_{α+α_i}-mod→H^Λ_α-mod as M↦u_{α,i}M and f_i as M↦H^Λ_{α+α_i}u_{α,i}⊗_{H^Λ_α}M. Mark biadjointness/exactness as supplied properties (not proved by the diagram), and mark H^Λ as a direct sum of supported content blocks; do not equate it with the full H_d(m) for finite proper I.
diagram_candidates.classification: Optional source-supported enhancement; no confirmed diagram error.

diagram_candidates.why: The theorem states explicit mutually inverse maps on each content sector, gives the direct-sum decomposition, and specifies generator images; these are naturally displayed as a pair of inverse maps.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: For each α draw R^Λ_α ⇄ H^Λ_α with ρ:R→H and σ:H→R and label σρ=id_R, ρσ=id_H, including zero sectors. Mark e(i)↦e(i), y_r↦y_r, ψ_r↦the stated intertwiner quotient; note the degenerate/nondegenerate dot images x_r−i_r and 1−q_H^(−i_r)X_r. Then show ⊕_αR^Λ_α≅H^Λ_d. Keep the central content sector distinct from any primitive-block assertion.
